pr_body: Adds a configuration option to raise/not raise floating containers on gaining focus (see also https://github.com/i3/i3/issues/2990).
pr_comments: As I'm quite unfamiliar with the code-base:  I'm really not sure about the positioning of the 'raise on click'.  But I'm in awe how fast a working implementation could be created (I'm an openbox user and trying slowly to replace it).
It looks like i3 ended up implementing this without a `raise_floating` directive. Perhaps we should do the same.

Hmm unsure on how this can be handled without a configuration option, as some people might prefer one of the behaviours.  It seemed to me that i3 simply reverted what appeared to be a mistaken commit.
Could you add some documentation in `sway.5.scd` please?
Thank you! Will do.
That will take me a little time, I'm trying to understand scdoc.
I installed the manpage locally and looked at it, it looks ok.

Please hold off merging the branch for now.

I've been using this branch for a bit and I'm getting a few focus related bugs (where the focus is still on windows behind the foregroung one, missing focus borders..).  I'm not sure if it's related to my configuration or my code. I'll investigate.
I found #2525 which is a problem not unlike this one...

Thanks for the review!
I'm also good with reworking the pr to do what i3 did (which means having no configuration and the focus raising off). Let's see what the others say, then the pr needs a little bit of cleanup (wip on one commit, the `container_is_floating()` might not be necessary, ...) before a merge.

I marked the pr as wip, because I managed to reproduce the steps from #2492 after all.

Experimenting with the following now:
```c
// If focused is floating, focused view's non-popups
if (focus && focus->view && is_floating) {
	bool has_subsurfaces = wl_list_length(&focus->view->surface->subsurfaces) > 0;
	c = floating_container_at(lx, ly, surface, sx, sy);
        // only switch to second container if focused container has no menus open
	if (!has_subsurfaces && c && c != focus) {
		return c;
	}
```

This feels a little like what other window managers do.. including oddities like "when the menu is closed, the focused window will not unfocus without another click".

* create two windows, one of the something like gnome-dictionary
* open a menu in gnome-dictionary overlapping the second window
* click something in the menu
* wriggle mouse a little
* focus should move to the second window, but does not
* unfocuses only on hitting root window, not when moving outside the menu area onto the second window

And then, the simple question for subsurfaces, I'm not sure on the rules here. Is this even a legal assumption? There could be other reasons for subsurfaces I'm not seeing.
"When there is/was a menu, let the window keep the focus"... I'd rather it only keep it as long as the pointer is within the surface (+ subsurfaces).
I apologize for the back and forth, I'll see what I can come up with.

[edit 1]
Log of wriggling the mouse pointer after selecting something from the menu:
```
2018-09-30 10:51:01 - [sway/tree/container.c:374] floating 0x11ab9a0 or focused 0x124c9f0: sub:1 sur:1 v:1
2018-09-30 10:51:01 - [sway/tree/container.c:383] Using focused 0x124c9f0
2018-09-30 10:51:01 - [sway/desktop/transaction.c:394] Transaction 0x124cbc0 committing with 1 instructions
2018-09-30 10:51:01 - [sway/desktop/transaction.c:264] Applying transaction 0x124cbc0
2018-09-30 10:51:04 - [sway/tree/container.c:374] floating 0x11ab9a0 or focused 0x124c9f0: sub:0 sur:1 v:1
2018-09-30 10:51:04 - [sway/tree/container.c:377] Using floating 0x11ab9a0
2018-09-30 10:51:04 - [sway/tree/container.c:374] floating 0x11ab9a0 or focused 0x124c9f0: sub:0 sur:1 v:1
2018-09-30 10:51:04 - [sway/tree/container.c:377] Using floating 0x11ab9a0
2018-09-30 10:51:04 - [subprojects/wlroots/types/wlr_output.c:810] Falling back to software cursor on output 'X11-1'
2018-09-30 10:51:34 - [sway/tree/container.c:374] floating 0x11ab9a0 or focused 0x124c9f0: sub:0 sur:1 v:1
2018-09-30 10:51:34 - [sway/tree/container.c:377] Using floating 0x11ab9a0
```
So the the focused `0x12` gets chosen until the click. After that the branch for the floating window `0x11` below is used. Nevertheless, the focus stays on `0x12`. There must still be some logic higher up the stack?

[edit]

Yes, there was a little bit of a higher level logic.

```c
void cursor_send_pointer_motion(struct sway_cursor *cursor
...
        // Find the node beneath the pointer's previous position
	//struct sway_node *prev_node = node_at_coords(seat, cursor->previous.x, cursor->previous.y, &surface, &sx, &sy);
	struct sway_node *prev_node = cursor->previous.node;
```

The previous node wasn't saved but was recalculated for the previous pointer position again.  The environment changed (the menu was closed) so the re-calculation returned a wrong previous node.

Note, that this might fix #2525 too for the non-floating case, if the check were to be expanded for the tiling case. (That is, if this is a valid way of handling it...)

[edit]
It does, but there is a slight oddness around re-focusing the the container with the menu.  It is not sufficient to have the cursor above the subsurface, it needs to be inside the main container it seems (unsure, I should not have lost the focus).
And as a second sidenote, it seems to be no longer possible to use a click to force focusing another container.

[edit]
I think the better check would be a fictional `in_surface = is_within_surface(focus, x, y)` which also handles subsurfaces. Unsure on how expensive that is.
I don't have nearly as much context for this problem as you do. You should make the call as to which behavior is best, and when you've done so and this PR is ready for code review, lmk.
Take as much time as you need and don't worry too much about getting it perfect or performant, unless it's obviously broken or very slow.
Thank you @SirCmpwn for the kind words, I will tag you for a review when I feel that confident that the implementation is something that I **want** to use. Until then, I'll just keep doing what I do.

@SirCmpwn I think it's ok enough for you to have a look. I threw gperf/perf at it, it doesn't seem too expensive (at least what I could gather), valgrind didn't shout at me much and I couldn't make it crash.
(I tested mostly in the nested X11 variant.)
Thanks!
Thanks @SirCmpwn, everyone!

issue_context.title: Rendering is inconsistent with cursor events
issue_context.body:
Follow on from #2494.

If you create `V[terminal gedit]`, resize gedit to be stupidly small, then open the `Open` menu in gedit, it appears over the terminal. If you then focus the terminal and move the cursor over the menu, the cursor events apply to the terminal instead of the menu.

Some suggestions for fixing are in the above PR.
comments: @RyanDwyer with #2709 merged, this is hopefully no longer an issue?

I still think rendering is inconsistent with pointer input, even if the particular issue explained above is fixed. We really need to take the input code and "reverse it" when writing the rendering code.

review_comments: This condition looks wrong, but I think it's right. If you've moved the mouse over the floating container and it's given focus but hasn't raised because `raise_floating` is disabled, this part of the code raises it on click. Maybe add a comment explaining why this is here.
I amended the second commit with a comment.
